label: Tool server for an AI assistant

questions.question: Which jobs should an assistant be able to do through the server?
questions.why: A few concrete jobs keep the first tool list small.

questions.question: Who should be allowed to connect to it?
questions.why: Caller identity affects access and setup.

questions.question: Which jobs can only read, and which actually change something?

exit_criteria: Name the first three jobs, callers and permitted effects.

questions.question: Will the assistant connect on your computer or over the network?
questions.why: Local and hosted connections have different setup.

questions.question: Whose account does the server use for the service?
questions.why: That person controls access and costs.

questions.question: How should you cut off a connection when it is no longer needed?
questions.why: Revocation is part of the access plan.

exit_criteria: Confirm local or hosted connection, ownership and how access can be revoked.

questions.question: What information must the assistant supply for each job?
questions.why: Required inputs prevent actions on the wrong item.

questions.question: What does success return so the assistant can tell the user what happened?
questions.why: A visible result supports a reliable confirmation.

questions.question: What should the caller do if the service is busy, unavailable or refuses access?
questions.why: The failure response needs a useful next step.

exit_criteria: Specify required inputs, visible outcomes and error behavior for each selected tool.

questions.question: Which harmless sample jobs can prove each read tool works?
questions.why: Safe sample outputs can be checked repeatedly.

questions.question: How can you show one caller cannot read another caller's records?
Which assistant should try a clean installation first?
questions.why: The install guide needs a real client check.

exit_criteria: Write verifiable read-only test cases plus a permissions and install check.
